name: TRUMP, JUSTICE.
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court clearly erred in refusing to sentence Mr. McGann to a recidivist life sentence, as neither disproportionate sentencing nor substantive due process arguments validated the lower court's decision.

name: ARMSTEAD, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court did not err in terminating parental rights because the petitioner knowingly and intelligently waived his right to counsel and failed to correct conditions of abuse and neglect despite multiple chances.

name: BUNN, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the case should have been set for oral argument and that the petitioner's equal protection rights argument should be fully addressed in a signed opinion, given the disparate treatment compared to the Lane case.

name: WALKER, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, arguing that while the circuit court erred in failing to credit the defendant for the full time served, the error was harmless because the defendant ultimately received full credit in Raleigh County.

name: WOOTON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Special Acts requiring Cabell County to include library and park funding on its excess levy proposals violate equal protection guarantees because they create a discriminatory classification among counties without a compelling state interest.

description: Concurred, argued that the 2018 amendment to the burglary statute has a constitutional defect because its title failed to provide proper notice of the removal of the 'of another' requirement, but agreed the defect was harmless in this specific case.

name: HUTCHISON JUSTICE
description: Concurred, arguing that the life recidivist sentence was constitutional and proportionate as all the petitioner's felony offenses involved violence, and the application of the 2020 recidivist statute did not violate ex post facto principles.

name: ARMSTEAD, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Hope Scholarship Act is constitutional as the West Virginia Constitution's "free schools" clause does not prohibit the Legislature from enacting additional educational initiatives, and the Act does not impinge on a child's fundamental right to education or improperly direct public funds.

name: JUSTICE WOOTON
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE HUTCHISON
description: Dissented, argued that the Hope Scholarship Act is unconstitutional because it violates the West Virginia Constitution's mandate for a system of free public schools, denies public education its preferred status, and fails strict scrutiny review by reducing public school funding.

name: HUTCHISON CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court completely lacked jurisdiction to review as-applied challenges to WVSSAC rules and clearly erred in finding the Residence-Transfer Rule facially unconstitutional, as it meets the rational basis test by promoting academics over athletics and does not violate equal protection.

name: JUSTICE WOOTON
description: Recused himself from the decision.

name: JUDGE COURRIER
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: HUTCHISON, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the mid-deliberation substitution of a discharged alternate juror violated Rule 24(c) and the trial court failed to take extraordinary precautionary measures to rebut the presumption of prejudice, thus abusing its discretion by denying a mistrial.

name: ARMSTEAD, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the defendant was not prejudiced by the substitution of an alternate juror and received a fair trial, therefore his convictions should be affirmed.

name: Wooton, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court's failure to re-administer the juror oath to the recalled alternate juror was a fundamental, structural error that rendered the conviction invalid, and that the petitioner did not waive his constitutional right to a twelve-person sworn jury.

name: ARMSTEAD, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that claims for excessive force by police officers must be analyzed under the specific search and seizure clause (Article III, Section 6) and not the broader due process clause (Article III, Section 10), and that Section 10 claims are redundant as Section 6 does not provide a private right of action for monetary damages.

name: JUSTICE ALAN D. MOATS
description: Other, not participating.

name: Armstead, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Judge Goldston's actions were an unlawful search and an unconstitutional exercise of executive power, warranting censure and a $1,000 fine.

name: WOOTON, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the conduct was a legal error warranting admonishment and a $1,000 fine, not censure, and that the court should defer more to the Judicial Hearing Board's recommendation.

name: JUSTICE HUTCHISON
description: Recused himself and did not participate in the decision of this case.

name: JUDGE JENNIFER P. DENT
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: HUTCHISON, Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that prior decisions (Hall and Divita) were incorrectly decided by automatically reversing revocation orders for an officer's failure to provide a blood test, and that a new test should evaluate the violation in the context of the entire record.

name: WOOTON, J.
description: Dissented, arguing that the majority's new point of law is a dangerous exercise in futility, improperly creates judicial restraints on a legislatively prescribed due process right, and may invite misapplication in future criminal DUI proceedings, especially given the imminent termination of the administrative revocation procedure.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE JENKINS
description: Dissented, arguing that defendants are entitled to a jury trial for public nuisance claims and that the 2015 Act should apply, allowing for non-party fault.

name: ARMSTEAD, Justice
description: Dissented, arguing that while a jury trial is necessary for intertwined claims, the majority erred by denying defendants' statutory right to allocate fault under the 2015 Act, which should apply to the claims.

name: JUSTICE HUTCHISON
description: Concurred, arguing that the majority opinion skillfully addresses defendants' concerns, upholds jury trial rights, and allows the Mass Litigation Panel flexibility to manage the complex opioid litigation.

name: JUSTICE WOOTON
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, arguing that the Panel's decision for a bench trial on public nuisance claims was not clearly erroneous, but dissented from the majority's analysis for interfering with the Mass Litigation Panel's authority.

name: WALKER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that an EPO is not a de facto search warrant and does not authorize law enforcement to search a home for firearms, and no other warrant exception applied to validate the entry and search.

name: ARMSTEAD, J.
description: Concurred that an EPO is not equivalent to search and seizure authority but dissented from reversing the conviction, arguing the record requires further development on whether there was implied consent for officers to enter the home.
